facts.fact: The aqueduct has a sequence of earlier channels/building campaigns. INAH records reconstruction ordered by Fray Antonio de San Miguel between 1785 and 1789 and 253 arches. Do not call 1785 its only original construction date.
facts.location: Acueducto de la Ciudad de Morelia record

facts.fact: Calzada Fray Antonio de San Miguel linked the city to the Guadalupe chapel at the present San Diego Temple, explaining its San Diego/Guadalupe alternate names.
facts.excerpt: Calzada de San Diego o Calzada de Guadalupe
facts.location: Calzada Fray Antonio de San Miguel record

facts.fact: The calzada record describes late-eighteenth-century stonework with benches and ash trees, and eighteenth/nineteenth-century summer houses around it.

The city record lists the garden popularly known as Las Rosas under Luis González Gutiérrez, and identifies the Conservatorio de Las Rosas and its earlier convent/college musical activity. The public garden and the institution are separate spaces.
facts.location: Urban plazas/gardens overview and Conservatorio de las Rosas record
